## Mental Synopsis
Ichika feels amused and mildly intrigued by the new tutor, treating the situation like a role she can observe and play with. She senses there might be gaps behind his confident front and quietly enjoys testing his reactions. For now, she wants to keep things light and teasing while watching whether he slips up.

# Itsuki Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Itsuki is cautious but hopeful, wanting to believe the tutor will help them finally stabilize their grades. She feels a budding sense of responsibility to evaluate his seriousness and hold him to proper standards. Her immediate wish is to see clear, structured guidance that reassures her this arrangement is truly reliable.

# Miku Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Miku feels shy and a little overwhelmed by the new presence, preferring to observe from the background. She is quietly scrutinizing whether the tutor actually understands the material better than she does. Secretly, she hopes he’ll be patient and not dismiss her hesitations or slow responses.

# Nino Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Nino is suspicious and bristling under the idea that some outsider has been brought in to “fix” them. She feels ready to pounce on any sign of incompetence or arrogance from the tutor. Right now, she wants to test his claims and, if he fails, push to get rid of him quickly.

# Yotsuba Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Yotsuba is excited and optimistic, eager to welcome the tutor and make him feel comfortable in their home. She feels a simple hope that this will be fun and that everyone will get along better because of it. In the short term, she just wants to be helpful and supportive, even if she doesn’t fully understand how the tutoring will work.

Event 1:
  Summary:
    The elevator opens directly into the Nakano penthouse as the tutor arrives for the very first session. The living room is a chaotic mix of schoolbooks, snack wrappers, and five very different sisters reacting to his introduction in their own ways: Nino immediately questions his credentials and throws out a pointed remark about “fake experts,” Itsuki asks him to outline a concrete study plan for the semester, Ichika lounges on the sofa and casually asks a few deceptively simple subject questions while smiling, Miku watches quietly from the side with her headphones around her neck, and Yotsuba excitedly rushes to welcome him and suggests they all sit down together for a “warm-up quiz.” Their attention converges on the tutor, waiting to see how he responds to the pressure and questions.

  Soft Conditions:
    - Everyone is still gathered in the Nakano penthouse living room.

Event 2:
  Summary:
    As the group settles at the table with textbooks and notebooks spread out, Nino “accidentally” chooses one of the most difficult problems from their current unit and asks the tutor to walk them through it on the spot, insisting that a real tutor should be able to explain it clearly step by step. Ichika, amused, subtly adds a related but trickier follow-up question to see if he contradicts himself. Itsuki quietly starts taking notes on his explanations to evaluate how systematic they are, while Miku opens her own textbook to the same page, following every line to see if he truly understands it. Yotsuba tries to ease the tension by suggesting small breaks or turning the question into a tiny game, but the room’s focus stays tightly on how the tutor handles this demonstration.

  Soft Conditions:
    - The group is still seated together at a table or study area inside the penthouse.

Event 3:
  Summary:
    During the ongoing session, a sudden notification arrives on the shared family tablet: their latest quiz scores from school have been posted, and they are bad enough that Their grandfather is automatically emailed a progress report. Nino seizes on this as proof that they can’t afford a useless tutor, pressing the issue more aggressively. Itsuki insists they immediately adjust their study strategy and asks the tutor to propose a concrete weekly schedule. Ichika, sensing rising tension, gently steers the conversation to whether they should “give this tutor a trial period,” while Miku quietly wonders if she should ask for one-on-one help later to see his true level. Yotsuba, flustered but upbeat, suggests some kind of group promise or pact to improve together, leaving the tutor under intensified scrutiny about whether he can rise to the challenge.

  Soft Conditions:
    - The sisters and tutor are still in the penthouse, with access to their school accounts or a device showing grades.

The elevator doors slid open with a soft chime directly into the Nakano penthouse, revealing polished floors half-hidden under a sprawl of open textbooks, loose worksheets, and a trail of empty snack wrappers that led toward the living room. The air smelled faintly of buttered popcorn and citrus cleaner, the late afternoon sun pouring in through the wide windows and splashing gold across the mess. Voices overlapped somewhere ahead—bickering, muffled, familiar to each other in a way that made any outsider feel very, very new.

On the far side of the living room, Ichika lay draped across the longest sofa like she’d grown there, one leg dangling over the edge, her yellow cardigan tied carelessly around her waist. She tilted her head as the new tutor stepped in, a slow, assessing smile curving her lips. “Ah, you must be our savior,” she said lightly, as if testing how the word sat on him. “Or are you more of a ‘barely-on-time transfer student who just remembered there was a test today’ type?” Her tone was playful, but her eyes watched his expression closely, measuring every flicker.

Itsuki sat upright at the low table, back straight, red vest perfectly in place despite the chaos around her. Her open notebook was already divided into neat sections, pens lined at attention. She closed a textbook with a quiet thump and rose to give a polite bow. “Thank you for coming,” she said, voice formal but not cold. “Since we’re starting mid-semester, I’d like to hear your study plan. For the whole term, if possible. Goals, methods, and how you intend to track our progress.” She clutched her notebook to her chest afterward, as though ready to record his answer verbatim.

Miku lingered near the armchair, half in shadow, her large headphones resting around her neck. She’d turned down the volume on whatever she’d been listening to, the screen of her phone gone dark in her hand. Her gaze flicked to him, then away, then back again, quietly scanning his face. She didn’t say anything at first, just nudged a history textbook with her foot so it was closer to the table and opened it to a dog-eared page. When she finally spoke, it was barely above a murmur. “We’re… pretty far behind,” she added, more to the floor than to him.

Nino stood near the kitchen counter, arms crossed, butterfly ribbons perfectly aligned in her pink hair like a warning sign. She didn’t bother to hide the way her eyes swept him from head to toe, sharp and unimpressed. “So this is the guy they picked?” she scoffed. “You don’t look like a genius. Or a teacher.” She picked up a crumpled worksheet, waving it like evidence. “Let me guess, you’re one of those ‘online tutoring experts’ with a flashy profile and nothing behind it? Because if you’re a fake, we don’t have time to waste on you.”

Yotsuba practically bounced into his personal space before the echo of Nino’s words had faded, her big green ribbon bobbing with each step. “Welcome, welcome!” she beamed, hands clasped behind her back as she rocked on her heels. “You made it all the way up here without getting lost, right? That’s already pretty impressive!” She spun toward the table, scooping up stray pencils as she went. “Let’s all sit down and do a warm-up quiz! Like… um… a mini test so you can see how bad we are, and we can see how awesome you are!” She looked back at him with open, hopeful eyes, clearly expecting him to grab hold of that idea and make it work.

The room’s attention closed in on him as the elevator doors slid shut behind his back with a definitive click. Ichika’s soft, amused gaze, Itsuki’s earnest scrutiny, Miku’s silent watchfulness, Nino’s open hostility, and Yotsuba’s eager encouragement all converged, waiting. Books lay open on the table like a gauntlet. Whatever he said or did next would be his first real test.
